subjects.name: United States Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases

summary: After the 2001 anthrax letter attacks in the United States, the FBI and the press spent years publicly targeting biodefense researcher Steven Hatfill, a man with an embellished resume and a Rhodesian past, without real evidence that he was responsible.

evidence.note: Hatfill's birth in 1953 in Missouri opens the biography
about a year volunteering at a mission hospital in the Congo
moves to white-ruled Rhodesia in 1978 to attend medical school
long segment on the Rhodesian military's chemical and biological weapons use in the Bush War
medical degree, internship and master's degrees in South Africa through the 1980s
false claims of UK medical credentials, a PhD and a faked Oxford reference
joins USAMRIID in 1997; description of the Fort Detrick biodefense lab
mentorship by bioweapons veteran Bill Patrick, holder of secret anthrax patents
builds a mock mobile bioweapons lab for SAIC; CIA and DoD clearance trouble in 2001

notes: Part 2 has no transcript; the investigation, media coverage and outcome (taken as 2001-2008, ending with his 2008 settlement) come from the description and general knowledge. Bruce Ivins is listed as a keyword on the assumption Part 2 covers the FBI's later suspect; check this. Primary theme could also be terrorism. The Richard Jewell episode named in the intro is a separate story.
